1.word_for_word: एकविंशे — in the twenty-first chapter; शरद्-रम्य-वृन्दावन-गते हरौ — when Hari entered Vṛndāvana made lovely by autumn; तद्-वेणु-स्वनम् आकर्ण्य — hearing the sound of his flute; गोपीभिः गीतम् ईर्यते — the song uttered by the gopīs is presented; इत्थम् — thus, in this condition; शरदा स्वच्छानि जलानि यस्मिन् — in which the waters were made clear by autumn; वायुना वतम् अनुगतम् — pervaded by the wind; तद्-एक-व्याप्तम् — filled throughout by it
1.translation: In the twenty-first chapter, when Hari entered Vṛndāvana made lovely by autumn, the song sung by the gopīs after hearing the sound of his flute is presented. ‘Ittham’ means ‘thus, in such a condition.’ The forest was such that its waters had been made clear by autumn and it was pervaded throughout by the moving wind.

2.word_for_word: कुसुमित-वन-राजिषु — among rows of flowering forest vegetation; शुष्मिणः मत्ताः भृङ्गाः — vigorous, intoxicated bees; द्विजाः खगाः च — and birds; तेषां कुलानि — their multitudes; तैः घुष्टाः — resounding with them; सरांसि सरितः महीध्राः च — lakes, rivers and mountains; तत् वनम् अवगाह्य प्रविश्य — entering deeply into that forest; कृष्णः वेणुम् अवादयत् — Kṛṣṇa played the flute
2.translation: The rows of forest trees were in flower, and the lakes, rivers and mountains resounded with swarms of vigorous, intoxicated bees and flocks of birds. Entering deeply into that forest, Kṛṣṇa played his flute.

3.word_for_word: तत् कृष्ण-वेणु-गीतम् — that song of Kṛṣṇa's flute; स्मरस्य उदयः यस्मात् — from which erotic love arose; तत् आश्रुत्य आकर्ण्य श्रुत्वा — hearing and receiving it through the ears; परोक्षं यथा भवति तथा — as something heard from a distance, not directly seen; व्रजे स्थितत्वात् — because they remained in Vraja
3.translation: They heard that song of Kṛṣṇa's flute, from which love arose in them. They heard it from a distance, without seeing him directly, because they themselves remained in Vraja.

4.word_for_word: विक्षिप्त-मनसः — whose minds were scattered; व्याकुल-चित्ताः — whose hearts were agitated and overwhelmed
4.translation: ‘Vikṣipta-manasaḥ’ means that their minds were scattered and their hearts overwhelmed with agitation.

5.word_for_word: यादृशं कृष्ण-स्मरणम् — the particular remembrance of Kṛṣṇa; तासां मनसः क्षोभकम् — which agitated their minds; बर्हापीडम् इति — expressed by the verse beginning 'barhāpīḍam'; नटवत् वरं वपुः बिभ्रत् — bearing a supremely beautiful body like an actor; वृन्दावनं प्राविशत् — he entered Vṛndāvana; स्व-पदैः अङ्कितैः — marked by his own footprints; रमणम् रति-जनकम् — charming, generating love; गोप-वृन्दैः गीत-कीर्तिः — whose fame was sung by groups of cowherds; बर्ह-मयम् आपीडम् — a crest-ornament made of peacock feathers; रन्ध्रान् वेणोः — the holes of the flute; अधर-सुधया एव पूर्णात् वेणोः — from the flute filled with the nectar of his lips; उच्चलन्ती गीतवत् प्रसर्पितुम् — flowing outward and spreading as song; अधिकः श्लोकः वीरराघव-संस्करणे — the following verse is additional in the Vīrarāghava recension
5.translation: The verse beginning ‘barhāpīḍam’ states the form of Kṛṣṇa-remembrance that so disturbed the gopīs' minds. Kṛṣṇa entered Vṛndāvana bearing a supremely beautiful body like an actor. The forest, marked by his own footprints, became delightful and love-awakening, while his glory was sung by groups of cowherds. He wore a crest made of peacock feathers; alternatively, the phrase may qualify his whole form as crowned with such a crest. The description of the flute is poetic suggestion: because the flute had been filled with the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, that nectar itself seemed to stream out through its holes and spread abroad in the form of song. The following metrical verse is an additional verse found in the Vīrarāghava recension.

6.word_for_word: अभिरेभिरे — they embraced; वर्णयन्त्यः पदे पदे — while describing him at every step/word; परमानन्द-मूर्तिम् कृष्णम् — Kṛṣṇa, the embodiment of supreme bliss; परिरब्धवत्यः — they embraced him
6.translation: As they described him, at every word they seemed to embrace Kṛṣṇa himself, the embodiment of supreme bliss. ‘Abhirebhire’ means ‘they embraced him.’

7.word_for_word: अनुवर्णनम् एव — this is the continuation of their description; अक्षण्वताम् इति त्रयोदशभिः — in thirteen verses beginning 'akṣaṇvatām'; अक्षण्वताम् चक्षुष्मताम् — of those possessing eyes; इदम् एव फलम् प्रिय-दर्शनम् — this alone is the fruit: seeing the beloved; परम् अन्यत् न विदामः — we know no higher fruit; सखिभिः सह पशून् वनं प्रवेशयतोः राम-कृष्णयोः वक्त्रम् — the faces of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa as they lead the cattle into the forest with their friends; यैः निपीतम् — by those whose eyes have drunk them in; तैः एव जुष्टम् — enjoyed by those alone; अनु-वेणु — following the flute; अनुरक्त-कटाक्ष-मोक्षम् — sending forth affectionate glances
7.translation: Their description continues for thirteen verses beginning with ‘akṣaṇvatām.’ For those who possess eyes, they say, this alone is their true fruit: the sight of the beloved; we know of no greater fruit. The faces of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, as they lead the cattle into the forest with their friends, are truly enjoyed only by those whose eyes drink them in. Kṛṣṇa's face follows the flute as he plays it, and he sends forth soft, affectionate sidelong glances. Alternatively, the construction is that those who have drunk in the two faces are precisely those who have enjoyed the true fruit of having eyes.

8.word_for_word: अन्या आहुः — other gopīs say; चूत-प्रवाल-आदीनाम् चित्राभिः मालाभिः — with variegated garlands of mango shoots and the like; अनुपृक्ते — interwoven here and there; परिधाने नील-पीत-अम्बरे — in their blue and yellow garments; विचित्रः वेषः — their dress was wonderfully variegated; पशुपाल-गोष्ठ्याम् मध्ये — in the midst of the assembly of cowherds; अलम् अत्यर्थं विरेजतुः — they shone exceedingly; अहो गोपानां पुण्यम् — ah, the merit of the cowherds!
8.translation: Other gopīs say: with variegated garlands of mango shoots and other forest ornaments interwoven here and there with their blue and yellow garments, the two brothers wore a wonderfully colorful dress. At times, standing in the very midst of the cowherd assembly, they shone with extraordinary beauty. The implied thought is: ‘Ah, how great is the merit of the cowherds!’

9.word_for_word: अयं वेणुः किं स्म पुण्यम् आचरत् — what merit did this flute perform; गोपिकानाम् एव भोग्याम् — meant to be enjoyed by the gopīs alone; दामोदर-अधर-सुधाम् — the nectar of Dāmodara's lips; स्वयं स्वातन्त्र्येण यथेष्टं भुङ्क्ते — it itself independently enjoys as much as it wishes; अवशिष्ट-रसम् — leaving only the remaining flavor; ह्रदिनीनां पयसा पुष्टः — nourished by the water of the lakes; ताः मातृ-तुल्याः ह्रदिन्यः — those lakes are like mothers to it; हृष्यत्-त्वचः — their skin bristling with joy; विकसित-कमल-वन-मिषेण रोमाञ्चिताः — appearing horripilated through blooming lotus beds; येषां वंशे जातः ते तरवः — the trees in whose bamboo lineage it was born; मधु-धारा-मिषेण आनन्द-अश्रु मुमुचुः — shed tears of joy in the form of streams of sap/honey; आर्याः कुल-वृद्धाः इव — like noble family elders; स्व-वंशे भगवत्-सेवकम् दृष्ट्वा — seeing a servant of Bhagavān born in their lineage
9.translation: Other gopīs ask: ‘What merit did this flute perform?’ Although the nectar of Dāmodara's lips is meant to be enjoyed by the gopīs alone, the flute independently drinks as much of it as it pleases, leaving only the residual taste for others. The lakes whose water nourished the bamboo are like its mothers; through the blossoming lotus beds they seem to bristle with delight. The trees of the bamboo's lineage shed streams of sap like tears of joy. They are like noble elders of a family who, seeing a servant of Bhagavān arise in their own lineage, thrill with joy and shed tears.

10.word_for_word: वृन्दावनं भुवः कीर्तिं स्वर्गात् अपि विशेषेण वितनोति — Vṛndāvana especially spreads the glory of the earth, surpassing heaven; देवकी-सुतस्य पदाम्बुजाभ्यां लब्धा लक्ष्मीः — it has received splendor from the lotus feet of Devakī's son; गोविन्दस्य वेणु-निनादं श्रुत्वा — hearing Govinda's flute; मन्द-गर्जितं नील-मेघं तं मत्वा — taking him to be a blue cloud with soft thunder; मत्ताः मयूराः नृत्यम् — intoxicated peacocks dance; तत् प्रेक्ष्य — seeing that; अन्यानि समस्तानि सत्त्वानि — all the other creatures; अद्रि-सानुषु — on the mountain slopes; उपरत-क्रियाणि — cease their activity; न एतत् अन्येषु लोकेषु विद्यते — nothing like this exists in other worlds
10.translation: Some say: ‘Friend, Vṛndāvana especially spreads the glory of the earth, even beyond heaven, because it has received the splendor bestowed by the lotus feet of Devakī's son. When the peacocks hear Govinda's flute they take him for a dark-blue cloud softly thundering and, intoxicated with joy, begin to dance. Seeing their dance, all the other creatures gathered on the mountain slopes stop whatever they are doing. Such a wonder does not exist in other worlds; therefore Vṛndāvana magnifies the glory of the earth.’

11.word_for_word: मूढ-मतयः तिर्यग्-जातयः अपि एताः हरिण्यः — even these deer, animal-born and supposedly dull-minded; धन्याः कृतार्थाः — are blessed and fulfilled; वेणु-रणितम् आकर्ण्य — hearing the flute's sound; नन्द-नन्दनं प्रति — toward Nanda's son; प्रणय-सहितैः अवलोकनैः — with loving glances; विरचितां पूजां संमानं दधुः — offered worship and honor; कृष्णसारैः स्व-पतिभिः सहिता एव — together with their black-deer husbands; अस्मत्-पतयः तु गोपाः क्षुद्राः — whereas our cowherd husbands are mean-minded; समक्षं तत् न सहन्ति — they would not tolerate such worship before their eyes
11.translation: Another gopī says: ‘Friend, even these deer—though born as animals and considered dull-minded—are blessed and fulfilled. Hearing the sound of the flute, they worship Nanda's son with loving glances, and they do so openly in the company of their own black-deer husbands. Our own cowherd husbands, by contrast, are so narrow-hearted that they would not tolerate our showing such devotion in their presence.’

12.word_for_word: वनितानाम् उत्सवः यस्मात् तत् रूपं शीलं च यस्य — whose form and conduct are a festival for women; कृष्णं निरीक्ष्य — seeing Kṛṣṇa; तेन वादित-वेणोः असङ्कीर्णं गीतं श्रुत्वा — hearing the pure, unmixed song of the flute he played; विमानैः गच्छन्त्यः देव्यः — celestial women traveling in aerial cars; देवानाम् अङ्केषु स्थिताः अपि — though seated in the laps of their divine husbands; स्मरेण नुन्न-साराः — their inner firmness struck away by love; परिक्षिप्त-धैर्याः — deprived of composure; मुमुहुः — became bewildered; भ्रश्यत्-प्रसूनाः कवराः — flowers fell from their hair-knots; विगता नीव्यः — their waist-knots loosened; वक्तृ-भेदात् न अतीव सङ्गतिः — because different gopīs are speaking, perfect continuity need not be demanded
12.translation: Another gopī says: ‘Hear something astonishing. Kṛṣṇa's form and character are themselves a festival for women. Celestial goddesses traveling in aerial cars, although seated in the laps of their divine husbands, see him and hear the pure flute-song he produces; struck by love, their inner firmness collapses and they become bewildered. The sign of that bewilderment is that flowers fall from their loosened hair and the knots of their garments come undone.’ Śrīdhara adds that, because different gopīs are speaking throughout this song, one should not demand an overly strict continuity between every statement.

13.word_for_word: क्षरण-शङ्कया एव उत्तम्भितैः कर्ण-पुटैः पिबन्त्यः — drinking with ears raised as if afraid the sound might spill away; शावाः च वत्साः च — calves and young animals; स्तन-पाने प्रवृत्ताः — engaged in drinking milk; गीतं श्रुत्वा — hearing the song; तत् एव पीयूषम् पिबन्तः — drinking that very nectar; स्नुत-स्तन-पयः-कवलाः — with mouthfuls of milk flowing from the teat; तस्थुः विस्मृत-क्रियाः — stood still, forgetting their activity; गोविन्दं दृशा मार्गेण आत्मनि मनसि स्पृशन्त्यः आलिङ्गन्त्यः — touching and embracing Govinda within the mind through the path of sight; अश्रूणां कला लेषाः लोचनेषु — traces of tears in their eyes
13.translation: The cows seemed to drink the sound with their ear-cavities raised, as though afraid that the nectar might spill away. The calves, already drinking from the teat, heard the flute-song and began drinking that nectar instead; with mouthfuls of milk still in their mouths they simply stood motionless, forgetting what they had been doing. The reason is that cows and calves alike touched and embraced Govinda inwardly, bringing him into the heart through the path of their gaze, and faint traces of tears appeared in their eyes.

14.word_for_word: भो अम्ब मातः — O mother; अस्मिन् वने ये विहगाः — the birds in this forest; प्रायेण मुनयः भवितुम् अर्हन्ति — must surely be sages; कृष्ण-ईक्षितम् कृष्ण-दर्शनम् — direct sight of Kṛṣṇa; पुष्प-फल-आदि-अन्तरं विना — without any intervening flowers, fruits or obstruction; रुचिराः प्रवालाः येषां द्रुम-भुजान् आरुह्य — climbing tree-branches with lovely shoots; श्री-कृष्णेन उदितं कल-वेणु-गीतम् — the sweet flute-song manifested by Śrī Kṛṣṇa; अमीलित-दृशः — with unblinking eyes; त्यक्त-अन्य-वाचः — abandoning all other sounds/speech; शृण्वन्ति — they listen; मुनयः — sages; वेद-उक्त-कर्म-फल-परित्यागेन — abandoning the fruits of Vedic ritual; वेद-द्रुम-शाखा-रूढाः — ascending the branches of the Veda-tree; कर्माणि एव उपाददानाः — retaining the rites themselves as supports; श्री-कृष्ण-गीतम् एव शृण्वन्ति — listen only to Kṛṣṇa's song
14.translation: ‘O mother! The birds in this forest must surely be sages. Why? They climb the arms of the trees, whose shoots are beautiful, and from there behold Kṛṣṇa directly, without flowers, fruits or anything else obstructing their sight. With unblinking eyes and all other cries abandoned, they listen only to the sweet flute-song manifested by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.’ The deeper comparison is this: sages abandon the promised fruits of Vedic rites, ascend the branches of the Veda-tree, and retain the rites only as supports appropriate to the path; delighting inwardly, they listen only to the song of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Therefore, the gopīs suggest, these birds deserve to be regarded as those very sages.

15.word_for_word: आस्तां चेतनानां कथा — leave aside the case of conscious beings; नद्यः अपि — even the rivers; आवर्तैः परिभ्रमैः लक्षितेन मनो-भवेन कामेन — by love indicated through their circling whirlpools; भग्नः वेगः यासाम् — whose onward current is broken; ऊर्मयः एव भुजाः — their waves themselves are arms; आलिङ्गनेन स्थगितम् — as though stopping him in an embrace; कमल-उपहारा — presenting lotuses as offerings; मुरारेः पाद-युगलं गृह्णन्ति — they seize and hold Murāri's pair of feet
15.translation: Leave aside conscious beings—even the rivers are overcome. Their love is indicated by their circling whirlpools, and under its force their forward current is broken. Their waves become arms with which they seem to stop Murāri in an embrace, while offering lotuses and holding fast to his two feet.

16.word_for_word: लोकार्ति-हरण-शीलत्व-आदि-साम्यात् — because of similarity in relieving the suffering of the world and similar qualities; सख्युः श्री-कृष्णस्य अम्बुदः — the cloud is a friend of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; तत्-उपरि उदितः — risen above him; प्रेम्णा प्रवृद्धः — swelling through love; कुसुमावलीभिः तुल्यैः तुषारैः — with droplets like clusters of flowers; स्व-वपुषा छत्रं विहितवान् — made its own body into an umbrella
16.translation: Because the cloud resembles Śrī Kṛṣṇa in such qualities as relieving the distress of the world, it is described as his friend. Rising above Kṛṣṇa and swelling with love, it scattered cool droplets like clusters of flowers and spread its own body over him as an umbrella.

17.word_for_word: साहङ्कारम् आहुः — they speak with a trace of proud envy; पूर्णाः कृतार्थाः — fulfilled, having achieved their purpose; पुलिन्द्यः — Pulinda women, tribal women; प्रथमं दयितानां स्तनेषु मण्डितेन — with kuṅkuma first adorning the breasts of Kṛṣṇa's beloveds; रति-समये उरुगायस्य पदाब्जयोः रागेण आरुण्येन — made red by contact with Śrī Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet during love-play; वन-स्थलीषु चङ्क्रमणेन तृणेषु रूषितेन — transferred to grasses as he walked through the forest; तत्-दर्शनेन स्मर-कृता रुक् तापः यासाम् — whose burning pain of love arose on seeing it; आननेषु कुचेषु च काम-तप्तेषु लिम्पन्त्यः — smearing it on their love-heated faces and breasts; तत्-आधिं जहुः — they cast off that anguish
17.translation: The gopīs speak with a touch of proud envy: ‘The Pulinda women are complete; they have attained their purpose.’ The kuṅkuma had first adorned the breasts of Kṛṣṇa's beloveds and, during amorous play, had colored Śrī Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet red. As he walked through the forest it rubbed onto the grass. Merely seeing that kuṅkuma awakened the Pulinda women's burning love; they smeared it on their heated faces and breasts and thereby cast off their anguish. Hence the gopīs call those women fulfilled, with the implied lament: ‘Shame on women such as us who cannot obtain even this remedy for our suffering.’

18.word_for_word: हन्त इति हर्षे — 'hanta' expresses delighted wonder; अयम् अद्रिः गोवर्धनः — this mountain Govardhana; हरि-दासेषु श्रेष्ठः — is the best among Hari's servants; राम-कृष्णयोः चरण-स्पर्शेन प्रमोदः यस्य — who rejoices at the touch of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa's feet; तृण-आदि-उद्गम-निभेन रोम-हर्ष-दर्शनात् — whose sprouting grasses resemble hairs standing on end; मानं तनोति — he extends honor; पानीयैः — with water; सूयवसैः — excellent grass; कन्दरैः — caves; कन्द-मूलैः — roots and tubers; सह गोभिः गणेन सखि-समूहेन — to them together with cows and groups of friends
18.translation: ‘Hanta’ expresses delighted wonder: ‘Friends, this mountain Govardhana is surely the best of Hari's servants.’ Why? He experiences joy from the touch of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa's feet, visibly manifesting horripilation in the form of grasses and other vegetation springing up over him. Moreover, he offers proper honor to the two brothers, together with their cows and groups of friends, by providing water, excellent grass, caves, roots and tubers. Thus this mountain is exceedingly blessed.

19.word_for_word: इदम् तु अति-चित्रम् — this is exceedingly wondrous; गोपैः सह वने वने गाः सञ्चारयतोः — as the two move from forest to forest tending cows with the cowherds; राम-कृष्णयोः मधुर-पदैः महा-वेणु-नादैः — by the sweet notes and powerful flute-sounds of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; शरीरिषु गतिमताम् अस्पन्दनम् — moving creatures become motionless; स्थावर-धर्मः — taking on the property of stationary beings; तरूणां पुलकः — the trees exhibit horripilation; जङ्गम-धर्मः — taking on a property of living moving beings; निर्योगाः — ropes used to bind or draw difficult cattle; पाद-बन्ध-रज्जवः — ropes binding the feet; स्कन्ध-स्थ-पाशेन — with a rope resting on the shoulder; गोप-परिवृढ-श्रिया विराजमानयोः — the two shine with the majesty of chief cowherds
19.translation: ‘Friends, this is especially astonishing. As Rāma and Kṛṣṇa move from forest to forest with the cowherds, tending the cows and sounding the flute in sweet, powerful notes, moving creatures become motionless, adopting the characteristic of stationary beings; meanwhile the trees bristle with horripilation, displaying a characteristic of sentient moving beings.’ Śrīdhara also glosses the cowherd equipment: ‘niryoga’ means the ropes used to bind the feet or to draw stubborn cattle. With such ropes wound at the head and carrying a noose upon the shoulder, the two brothers shone with the majesty of foremost cowherd leaders. The explanation continues through verse 20.
